joan: Uploaded new partner sheet from ACME. They included commit amounts, a credit bucket, and a vague "preempt_mix" column. Need to normalize for the cost model. @liam can you lead ingest?

acct-bot: new file: acme_commit_v2.csv (s3://partner-ingest/acme/acme_commit_v2.csv) :file_folder:

liam: on it. quick scan shows varied phasing windows (1,3,6 mo) and some rows have preempt_mix=\"hi\", some numeric like 0.4, and a few blank.

nadeem: for blanks let's default to partner-stated supply fraction if present, else fall back to proxy mapping. I suggest proxy mapping low=15%, med=35%, high=65% (more conservative than last time).

priya: finance will want the amortization behavior clearly separated from billing treatment. propose we output both: (a) amortized-credit schedule for P&L and (b) instant gross reduction view that product can use for real-time routing sims.

liam: agreed. ingest plan: 1) normalize preempt_mix: if numeric use as-is (cap between 0 and 1), else map words to proxy; 2) expand credit_pool_usd into monthly amortized rows according to phasing_months; 3) add latency_premium_ms from notes column or default 0 and flag as estimated; 4) generate a GL-friendly export.

joan: also flag rows where apply_to_reserved_only=true vs false — partner's sheet mixes both. That changes how credits flow through our reserved-ephemeral accounting.

liam: header sample I'm pasting to be explicit: ```csv
vendor_sku,region,commit_tier,commit_rate_per_hour_usd,credit_pool_usd,phasing_months,preempt_mix,apply_to_reserved_only,notes
ACME-80GB-A,us-east,large,0.50,75000,3,,false,"latency_premium=5ms"
```

nadeem: edge-case: commit_rate_per_hour_usd missing on some rows. For those, fallback to our catalog floor for that sku+region and mark as imputed.

priya: scenarios finance wants: Conservative = use partner numeric if given, otherwise proxy mapping; amortize credits over phasing window; assume credits only offset reserved usage unless apply_to_reserved_only=false. Aggressive = apply full credit immediately across reserved+ephemeral and bump partner preemptible supply +25 percentage points (cap at 100%).

joan: can we also compute per-GPU-hour impact and per-million-token discount? product asks those for sizing the pricing ask.

liam: quick sample calc here for visibility: if commit_rate = $0.50/hr, credit_pool = $75,000 over 3 months, expected reserved units = 500 GPUs evenly used, amortized hours = 3 months * 30 days/month * 24 hrs/day * 500 GPUs = 1,080,000 GPU-hrs. Discount per GPU-hr = 75000 / 1,080,000 ≈ $0.06944/hr. Put differently, at a token emission baseline of 0.05 tokens/sec per GPU (≈180 tokens/hr), discount per-million-tokens ≈ (0.06944 / 180) * 1e6 ≈ $385.8 per million tokens — we'll format properly in the workbook.

nadeem: that token calc assumes all tokens are billed equally; we'll add variant rows for 8k/32k footprints and for batching effects.

liam: ETA: I'll drop transformed CSV, GL export, and two scenario worksheets (Conservative/Aggressive) to s3 by EOD PST. I'll also produce a short README listing all imputed mappings (preempt proxies, catalog fallbacks, latency defaults).

acct-bot: transformed dataset uploaded: acme_commit_v2_normalized.csv (s3://partner-ingest/acme/acme_commit_v2_normalized.csv)

joan: thanks. small ask from product: include a boolean column `proxy_used` when any default mapping or imputation was applied. Helps the pricing doc call out risky rows.

liam: will add proxy_used and a free-text `assumptions` column per row.

vendor-acme: FYI we can provide a more granular daily preempt profile if that helps — can share next week.

priya: perfect — ask them for daily or weekly preempt curves; that'll improve our batching and KV-cache planning.

joan: great progress. tag me when the workbook is live. Also capture latency premiums per-region in the output so routing sims can include them. :thumbsup:

liam: done and linked in s3. last_message_ts=2812345899

priya: finance will review tomorrow morning and send comments on the GL layout.Thanks everyone.
